high.title: Vietnam Stock Market Plunges Nearly 50 Points After "Free Fall" - What's Next?
high.summary: The Vietnamese stock market opened the new week negatively with VN-Index plummeting nearly 50 points to close around 1,790 points on June 8. This marked the deepest decline since late March and pulled the main index to its lowest level in nearly 2 months. Despite significantly discounted valuations after the correction, bottom-fishing flows remained cautious. Liquidity didn't surge dramatically during the selloff, with matched orders only around VND 16,000 billion, showing investor sentiment still leaning toward defense rather than aggressive buying. For FX and bond traders, this equity selloff reflects broader risk-off sentiment that could spill over into VND weakness and potential safe-haven demand for government bonds, though domestic institutional buying may provide some support.

high.title: VN-Index "Evaporates" Nearly 50 Points, Investors Await Critical Event Next Week
high.summary: VN-Index just experienced its sharpest decline in nearly 3 months, losing nearly 50 points and breaking through the 1,800-point level. The selloff occurred amid widespread "risk-off" sentiment in global financial markets as investors increasingly worry the Federal Reserve may maintain high interest rates longer than expected, not ruling out the possibility of rate hikes again. Nguyen The Minh from An Binh Securities noted Vietnam's stock decline is synchronized with global market corrections amid risk-off conditions. Most notably last week was the sharp rise in US Treasury yields and the DXY index amid market concerns about returning inflation pressure. This is the main reason why global stock markets corrected simultaneously. For VND traders, rising US yields and a stronger dollar create headwinds for emerging market currencies including the VND.

high.title: Gold Prices for Plain Rings and Bars Evening of June 8 Suddenly Drop Very Sharply
high.summary: Domestic gold prices continued to plummet in the late afternoon of June 8, extending sharp declines from early afternoon. Compared to the previous session's close, many brands reduced prices by up to VND 7.4 million per tael, bringing gold bars and plain gold rings down to the VND 143 million per tael range for selling prices - the lowest level in many months. At 4:45 PM, gold bars at SJC, PNJ, DOJI, Bao Tin Minh Chau and Bao Tin Manh Hai were all quoted at VND 138.8-143.8 million per tael (buy-sell). This dramatic gold price decline of 20% from recent peaks creates significant volatility in the VND gold market and may impact broader FX dynamics as investors reassess safe-haven demand.

medium.title: Losses of Those Who Bought Gold on God of Wealth Day
medium.summary: Gold continues declining from last week. At 4:30 PM, major brands quoted gold at VND 138.8 million (buy) and VND 143.6 million (sell) per tael. Those who bought on God of Wealth Day (Feb 26) at VND 184 million per tael now face losses of VND 45.2 million per tael. This highlights the volatility in Vietnam's gold market and potential impact on domestic savings behavior.

medium.title: Rare Phenomenon Many People Witness for First Time in Vietnam Gold Market
medium.summary: Gold prices had a strong "evaporation," dropping 7-9 million VND per tael. The spread between world gold prices and domestic selling prices narrowed to just 4-7 million VND per tael, compared to 12 million VND per tael on June 7. This convergence is rare in Vietnam's gold market and suggests improved arbitrage conditions.

medium.title: Multiple Board Members of One Bank Request Resignation
medium.summary: Eximbank will hold an extraordinary shareholders meeting on July 24, 2026 to consider board and supervisory board personnel matters. The bank received resignation requests from board members Pham Tuan Anh, Nguyen Tri Trung, and Nguyen Trong Hien. This governance change at a major bank could impact market confidence in the banking sector.

medium.title: Educational Sector Tycoon Accumulates Additional 102 Million ACB Shares in Just 2 Months
medium.summary: A group related to Ms. Ngo Thu Thuy increased ACB holdings from 257.4 million shares (5.01%) in late March to approximately 360 million shares (over 7%) by June 1. The accumulation of over 102 million shares worth around VND 2,300 billion occurred ahead of ACB's dividend payment plan of 20% (7% cash, 13% stock).
